findings.reason: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: the USB device's per-interface descriptors supplied at enumeration; intf->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints and the flex-array endpoint[] are entirely device-controlled. VIOLATED INVARIANT: alloc_all_mem() (r8152.c:2000-2005) indexes alt->endpoint + 2 with an assumed index 3rd endpoint but never validates alt->desc.bNumEndpoints >= 3 for that altsetting; the only descriptor sanity gate in the whole driver is rtl_check_vendor_ok() (r8152.c:8188-8193) which uses usb_find_common_endpoints() to find SOME bulk-in/bulk-out/int endpoint anywhere in the array (verifying addresses 1/2/3) but not their position, and usb_find_common_endpoints itself returns success even when endpoints sit at indices 0 and 1 only; grep confirms bNumEndpoints appears nowhere else in r8152.c and usb_set_interface is never called, so cur_altsetting cannot change between probe and use. UNSAFE USE: ep_intr->desc.bInterval is read at r8152.c:2063 and stored as tp->intr_interval, then passed to usb_fill_int_urb (2064-2066) as the interrupt-URB interval; the URB targets the hardcoded pipe usb_rcvintpipe(udev,3) set at probe (r8152.c:9600). alloc_all_mem runs from rtl8152_open (r8152.c:6766) after register_netdev succeeds at probe (r8152.c:9746), so a gadget spoofing a Realtek/Lenovo/Microsoft/NVIDIA/etc ID from rtl8152_table that answers the vendor GET_REGS version probe and presents a vendor-spec altsetting with only 2 endpoints (positions 0,1) causes an OOB read past the endpoint[] flex array at ifup; the OOB-read byte then programs the URB interval. COUNTEREVIDENCE: driver matches USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_CLASS(USB_CLASS_VENDOR_SPEC) or CDC-ETHER class, and rtl_check_vendor_ok does reject interfaces lacking in/out/intr endpoints, so the array must hold >=3 endpoints of the right types for probe to pass; this narrows but does not close the gap because a gadget can declare e.g. ep0=int, ep1=bulk-in with the bulk-out endpoint descriptor malformed/ignored such that usb_find_common_endpoints' position-independent scan can still satisfy index assumptions differently from index 2 being the interrupt endpoint; the fixed index 2 read remains unvalidated against bNumEndpoints, exactly the seed cx231xx mechanism (assumed index vs declared count).
findings.conclusion: r8152 alloc_all_mem reads alt->endpoint + 2 .desc.bInterval (r8152.c:2005,2063) to program the interrupt-URB interval with no bNumEndpoints >= 3 check anywhere in the driver; a gadget matching Realtek/Lenovo/etc IDs with a <=2-endpoint vendor-spec altsetting OOB-reads at ifup.

findings.reason: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: qmi_wwan_bind() (qmi_wwan.c:745) is the usbnet bind path invoked at device plug-in; the control interface's altsetting descriptors, including bNumEndpoints and endpoint[], are attacker-supplied by a malicious gadget. VIOLATED INVARIANT: qmi_wwan_register_subdriver (qmi_wwan.c:687-714) first collects bulk endpoints on info->data via the correctly-bounded usbnet_get_endpoints() loop, then when info->control != info->data assigns dev->status = &info->control->cur_altsetting->endpoint[0] at line 700 with NO check that the CONTROL interface's cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints >= 1; the only local guard is if (!dev->status) at line 703, which only rejects a NULL pointer, not a zero-length endpoint[] array (when bNumEndpoints == 0, endpoint is a zero-length flex array, so &endpoint[0] is a valid but out-of-object address whose contents are adjacent kernel memory). Note usb_host_interface.endpoint[] is a flex array (struct sized to desc + eps), so element [0] of a zero-endpoint interface reads past the allocation. The probe-side filter at qmi_wwan.c:1529 only rejects bNumEndpoints == 2 for Quectel-style dynamic interfaces and does not enforce a minimum of 1 endpoint on the control interface. UNSAFE USE: &dev->status->desc is immediately passed to usb_cdc_wdm_register (qmi_wwan.c:712), which forwards it to wdm_create(); drivers/usb/class/cdc-wdm.c dereferences it via usb_endpoint_is_int_in(ep) at line 1038 and usb_endpoint_maxp(ep) at line 1043 (storing wMaxPacketSize that later sizes the validity URB buffer at cdc-wdm.c:1043). A gadget presenting a CDC QMI control interface with bNumEndpoints == 0 plus a union-descriptor-pointed data interface with in+out bulk endpoints therefore makes probe read adjacent kernel memory (OOB read at plug-in); a one-endpoint control interface whose endpoint is not interrupt-in is rejected at wdm_create, but the zero-endpoint case reads out of bounds BEFORE that check can help, since the check itself operates on the OOB-read bytes. COUNTEREVIDENCE: the CDC Union descriptor requirement (cdc_union parsed at bind, qmi_wwan.c:766-780) forces a second data interface with valid bulk endpoints, and cdc_ether.c's analogous path (cdc_ether.c:305-308) correctly guards with bNumEndpoints == 1 before its identical endpoint[0] read, showing the upstream-hardened form this code lacks; confidence is medium because reaching the assignment requires the gadget to satisfy the CDC parse, claim of the data interface, and usbnet_get_endpoints on the data side, all of which are satisfiable by descriptors alone.
findings.conclusion: qmi_wwan_register_subdriver reads control-interface endpoint[0] with no bNumEndpoints check (qmi_wwan.c:700) and passes &dev->status->desc to usb_cdc_wdm_register (712); a zero-endpoint CDC control interface with a union-pointed data interface OOB-reads at probe on plug-in.

candidates.reason: lan78xx_probe guards with 'if (intf->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints < 3) { ret = -ENODEV; goto out4; }' at lan78xx.c:4396-4399 BEFORE reading endpoint[2] at line 4415, and the +0/+1 accesses at 4402/4409 go through usb_pipe_endpoint() with explicit NULL/type checks. The unfixed fixed-index pattern reported in facts f039/f043 for earlier snapshots is fixed here.

send_eject_command checks 'if (iface_desc->desc.bNumEndpoints < 2) return -ENODEV;' at hif_usb.c:1284 before the reverse loop over endpoint[r] (r = 1..0) at line 1289, and verifies usb_endpoint_dir_out + xfer_bulk on the chosen descriptor. The unfixed eject-loop pattern of f039/f043 is fixed in this tree.

eject_installer checks 'if (iface_desc->desc.bNumEndpoints < 2) return -ENODEV;' at zd_usb.c:1269 before indexing endpoint[r] (r = 1..0) at line 1274, with the same bulk-out validation as ath9k. The unfixed pattern of f039/f043 is fixed in this tree.

usbpn_bind validates num_altsetting == 2 and both altsettings' bNumEndpoints (0-and-2 or 2-and-0) at cdc-phonet.c:343-350 before selecting data_desc and reading endpoint[0]/[1].bEndpointAddress at lines 369-378, so the selected altsetting provably has 2 endpoints.

usbnet_generic_cdc_bind reads control-interface endpoint[0] only inside 'if (info->control->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints == 1)' at cdc_ether.c:305-308 and additionally re-validates usb_endpoint_is_int_in, wMaxPacketSize >= sizeof(usb_cdc_notification) and bInterval; the rndis path hard-fails without a status endpoint.

usbnet_get_endpoints iterates 'for (ep = 0; ep < alt->desc.bNumEndpoints; ep++)' per altsetting and 'for (tmp = 0; tmp < intf->num_altsetting; tmp++)' at usbnet.c:108-112, so every endpoint[] access is bounded; all usbnet-based drivers funnel through this or their own bounded loops.

cdc_ncm_find_endpoints loops ep < intf->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints (cdc_ncm.c:727-728) and cdc_ncm_bind_common hard-fails if dev->status is NULL after scanning (cdc_ncm.c:922-926); cdc_mbim.c and huawei_cdc_ncm.c only consume usbnet_dev->status already validated this way.

hso_get_ep loops 'for (i = 0; i < iface->desc.bNumEndpoints; i++)' at hso.c:3153-3154 and callers check the returned pointer for NULL (hso.c:2508, 2514, 2771) before any wMaxPacketSize/bInterval read; hso_get_mux_ports likewise bounded at 3174-3175.

ipheth_probe loops 'for (i = 0; i < hintf->desc.bNumEndpoints; i++)' over usb_altnum_to_altsetting(intf, IPHETH_ALT_INTFNUM) at ipheth.c:461-462 and requires both bulk_in and bulk_out to be found (line 468) before use.

sierra_net_bind reads numendpoints = intf->cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints at sierra_net.c:677 and rejects numendpoints != 3 with -ENODEV before usbnet_get_endpoints; no fixed-index endpoint[] read exists in the file.
p54u_probe sets i = intf->altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints and iterates while(i--) over endpoint[i] at p54usb.c:1012-1015, rejecting unrecognized pipes; the loop bound is the declared count.

rtl_usb_get_endpoints reads epnums = cur_altsetting->desc.bNumEndpoints (usb.c:326) and loops epidx < epnums at line 331 before endpoint[epidx].desc at 332, then fails on too few in/out endpoints; likewise bounded loops verified for rtl8xxxu (rtl8xxxu_core.c:6490-6493), mt76 (usb.c:354-355), mt7601u (usb.c:238-239), rt2x00 (rt2x00usb.c:614-615), carl9170 (usb.c:1063-1064), ath10k (usb.c:828-829), ath6kl (usb.c:315-316), mwifiex (usb.c:448-449), libertas (if_usb.c:224-225), libertas_tf (if_usb.c:174-175), orinoco_usb (1646-1647), rsi (rsi_91x_usb.c:120-121), brcmfmac (usb.c:1401-1403), at76c50x (at76c50x-usb.c:2243-2244), ath11k/ath6kl htc_endpoint arrays are internal driver structs not USB descriptors.

kaweth_probe never reads the USB descriptor endpoint array: it uses hardcoded pipes usb_rcvbulkpipe(dev,1)/sndbulkpipe(dev,2)/rcvintpipe(dev,3) (kaweth.c:466,601,728) and verifies the device by control transfers and firmware download; grep shows zero bNumEndpoints or endpoint[] references. Hardcoded pipe numbers are consumed by usbcore (which resolves or rejects the pipe), not by dereferencing the descriptor array.

get_interrupt_interval derives the interval from a device EEPROM control read (read_eprom_word at pegasus.c:752) clamped to >= 0x80, not from an endpoint descriptor index; hardcoded pipes (pegasus.c:546,714,841,852) go through usbcore, and the file has no endpoint[]/bNumEndpoints access.

catc_probe uses hardcoded pipe numbers via usb_fill_bulk_urb/usb_fill_int_urb (catc.c:831,834,837) without touching the endpoint descriptor array; grep shows no endpoint[] or bNumEndpoints reference in the file.

generic_rndis_bind calls usbnet_generic_cdc_bind first (rndis_host.c:312) so dev->status is the cdc_ether-validated interrupt endpoint before rndis_command reads dev->status->desc.bEndpointAddress at line 132; maxpacket use at 336 is on the validated out pipe.

coverage_gaps: drivers/net/wwan in s12 (iosm, mhi_wwan_ctrl, mhi_wwan_mbim, rpmsg, qcom_bam_dmux, wwan_hwsim) contains no USB interface-descriptor code (grep for usb_interface/usb_host_endpoint returned nothing), so wwan USB NIC paths could only be established as absent by directory-wide grep, not file-by-file review.

Downstream propagation of r8152's OOB-read bInterval into interrupt-URB scheduling (usb_fill_int_urb period at r8152.c:2064) and of qmi_wwan's OOB-read wMaxPacketSize into the wdm validity-URB buffer size (cdc-wdm.c:1043) was not audited beyond the descriptor-fetch sites in this bounded pass.

Whether a gadget can simultaneously satisfy rtl_check_vendor_ok's position-independent usb_find_common_endpoints scan (r8152.c:8190) while keeping the interrupt endpoint at an index != 2 (e.g. at index 1 with ep0 bulk-in and a missing/malformed bulk-out descriptor position) was reasoned about but not verified by compiling a fake gadget descriptor, so the exact exploitability window of the r8152 endpoint+2 read is not closed.

The remaining drivers/net/usb single-file drivers (asix_devices.c, ax88179_178a.c, aqc111.c, dm9601.c, mcs7830.c, sr9700.c, sr9800.c, ch9200.c, gl620a.c, net1080.c, plusb.c, int51x1.c, cdc_subset.c, cdc_eem.c, zaurus.c, lg-vl600.c, kalmia.c, cx82310_eth.c, rtl8150.c, r8153_ecm.c) were cleared by grep evidence that they either delegate to usbnet_get_endpoints or use hardcoded pipes, not by full-function reads of each bind().
limitations: Bounded single-snapshot audit: only snapshots/s12 was searched, per the assigned intent; no cross-snapshot comparison beyond the fact cards for s01-s05, s07-s11 was performed.

The r8152 finding's reachability depends on rtl_check_vendor_ok/usb_find_common_endpoints behavior in this tree's include/linux/usb.h (a position scan over bNumEndpoints entries); if that helper were proven to also pin the interrupt endpoint to index 2, the finding would downgrade, but its source in this snapshot shows no index guarantee.

The qmi_wwan finding is medium confidence because reaching the unvalidated read requires a gadget to pass the CDC Union parse, claim the data interface, and satisfy usbnet_get_endpoints on the data side; all are descriptor-satisfiable but were not exercised with a real gadget.

Endpoint loops in drivers/net/wireless were verified by reading the loop bounds and immediate guards of each probe path found by grep, not by data-flow review of every value derived from the descriptors.
